Download smaller than the app? That is normal — see “How delta updates work” below.
No delta patch was published for this version
The developer only uploaded the full APK for this update, so the full file is downloaded.
Your install is made of split APKs
Delta patches can only be applied to a single-file APK. Your app was installed as multiple parts, so the full APK is used.
A patch needs your current APK as its starting point. Android did not let the app read it, so the full APK is used.
Your installed build is not the one the patches were made for
Patches are made from one exact previous build. If you skipped versions, switched channels or installed from another source, they do not match, so the full APK is used.
The patch file did not contain the expected information, so it was ignored and the full APK is used.
The delta patch could not be downloaded
The small patch failed to download (network or GitHub issue), so the app falls back to the full APK.
Rebuilding the APK from the patch failed
Applying the patch on your device did not work, so the app falls back to the full APK.
The rebuilt APK failed the integrity check
The rebuilt file did not match the expected SHA-256 checksum, so it was thrown away and the full APK is used. This protects you from a broken or tampered file.
The rebuilt APK has a different signature
Android only updates an app with a file signed by the same key. The signature did not match, so the full APK is used.

Instead of downloading the whole app again, a delta update downloads only the parts that changed between your installed version and the new one — a small “patch” file. The app then rebuilds the complete new APK on your device from your current APK plus the patch. That is why the download can be much smaller than the app itself, and why you may see a short “Rebuilding…” step after it.\n\nIf a patch cannot be used for any reason, the app automatically downloads the full APK instead. The reason is always shown above, so a bigger download is never a mystery.
Safe by design: the rebuilt file is checked against a SHA-256 checksum and must carry the same signature as your installed app, otherwise it is discarded.
